panels.title: Targets down
panels.description: Core scrape targets that are not UP.

panels.title: Days to full
panels.description: Linear 6h forecast. Less than 7 days is red.

panels.title: SMART failures
panels.description: Drives reporting SMART overall-health failure.

panels.title: OOM containers
panels.description: Running containers currently marked OOMKilled.

panels.title: Certificate days
panels.description: Days until the earliest Traefik certificate expires.

panels.title: Last speedtest
panels.description: Age of the most recent internet speed test.

panels.title: CPU by core
panels.description: Per-core utilisation. A single pinned core can be hidden by total CPU usage.

panels.title: CPU states
panels.description: iowait and steal are the first signs of storage or virtualisation contention.

panels.title: Load per CPU
panels.description: Load normalised by logical CPU count. Above 1 means runnable work is waiting.

panels.title: Memory breakdown
panels.description: available is the number that matters; free excludes reclaimable cache.

panels.title: Swap I/O
panels.description: Sustained swap I/O is a memory-pressure signal even when swap usage is low.

panels.title: System temperature
panels.description: Requires lm-sensors and a loaded sensor driver. Telegraf is configured to normalise temp1_input to temp_input.

panels.title: Filesystem usage
panels.description: All mounted filesystems. Select specific mounts with the Mount variable.

panels.title: Inode usage
panels.description: Inodes can be exhausted while a filesystem still reports free bytes.

panels.title: Free space
panels.description: Free bytes per mounted filesystem. Filtered to real filesystems, not tmpfs or container overlays.

panels.title: Days to full
panels.description: Linear 6h growth forecast. A filesystem that is not shrinking shows a very large value.

panels.title: Disk latency
panels.description: Average I/O wait time per request. Throughput can look healthy while latency is high.

panels.title: Disk utilisation
panels.description: Percentage of time the device had I/O in flight. Sustained 100% means saturation.

panels.title: Disk queue depth
panels.description: I/O requests issued and not yet completed. A rising queue means the device is falling behind.

panels.title: SMART health
panels.description: Overall SMART health. Any FAIL is actionable.

panels.title: SMART temperature
panels.description: Drive temperature from smartctl. Watch for sustained temperatures above the drive's rated maximum.

panels.title: SMART error counters
panels.description: Reallocated, pending, uncorrectable and CRC errors. Values should stay flat; any increase deserves investigation.

panels.title: SMART wear
panels.description: SSD endurance indicators where the drive exposes them. HDDs normally have no data here.

panels.title: ARC hit ratio
panels.description: Overall ARC hit ratio. Falling below ~0.9 means more reads are reaching the disks.

panels.title: ARC vs RAM
panels.description: ZFS uses most free RAM by design; this is informational, not a capacity warning.

panels.title: Top containers by memory vs limit
panels.description: A container close to its own memory limit can be OOM-killed even when the host looks healthy.

panels.title: Container uptime
panels.description: Low uptime identifies containers that are restarting or crash-looping.

panels.title: Interface errors and drops
panels.description: Non-zero and rising errors usually mean a cable, NIC, driver or switch problem.

panels.title: TCP retransmits
panels.description: System-wide TCP retransmissions. Sustained values indicate packet loss or congestion.

panels.title: Internet speed
panels.description: Ookla speedtest results, scraped hourly.

panels.title: Internet latency
panels.description: Internet latency from the speedtest exporter.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: A dashboard with failed scrapes is lying to you. Check this first.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Rising scrape duration means exporters or Prometheus are under pressure.

panels.title: Prometheus TSDB series
panels.description: Unchecked cardinality growth eventually exhausts memory and disk.

panels.title: Open connections (Traefik)
panels.description: Currently open connections handled by Traefik, by entrypoint and protocol.

panels.title: Incoming requests by status
panels.description: Incoming HTTP requests through Traefik grouped by response class. A rising 5xx line is a service failure; a rising 4xx line can be scanning or auth failures.

panels.title: Top routers by request rate
panels.description: Which Traefik routers are receiving the most incoming requests.

panels.title: Top services by request rate
panels.description: Which backend services are receiving the most incoming requests.

panels.title: Listening TCP sockets
panels.description: TCP sockets in LISTEN state. Unexpected listeners are worth investigating.

panels.title: Half-open connections
panels.description: Connections in SYN_RECV state. Sustained growth can indicate a SYN flood or slow handshakes.

panels.title: Host TCP established
panels.description: All established TCP sockets on the host, including outbound connections. For HTTP-specific ingress use the Traefik panels above.
